title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 15
statement:
A container has a \(1 \times 1\) square bottom, a \(3 \times 3\) open square top, and four congruent trapezoidal sides, as shown. Starting when the container is empty, a hose that runs water at a constant rate takes \(35\) minutes to fill the container up to the midline of the trapezoids.

How many more minutes will it take to fill the remainder of the container?

solutions.text:
At height fraction \(t\) the square cross-section has side \(1 + 2t,\) so the volume filled up to height \(t\) is \(\int_0^t (1 + 2u)^2\,du.\) Up to the midline \(\left(t = \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\) this is \(\tfrac{7}{6},\) and the full volume is \(\tfrac{13}{3}.\) The remaining volume is \(\tfrac{13}{3} - \tfrac{7}{6} = \tfrac{19}{6},\) which is \(\tfrac{19}{7}\) times the first part. So the remainder takes \(35 \cdot \tfrac{19}{7} = 95\) more minutes.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: At height fraction \(t\) the cross-section is a square of side \(1 + 2t,\) so its area is \((1 + 2t)^2\)
Compare the volume up to the midline (\(t = \tfrac{1}{2}\)) with the total volume; fill time is proportional to volume
